---
title: Writing pages
description: The Markdown that smalldocs reads, each feature with its source and its result.
order: 3
---

A page is a Markdown file. smalldocs reads [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org), the standard form of
Markdown. It also reads some additions to Markdown, which this page describes:

- front matter, the options of the page at its top
- attributes, which give an id, classes or a width to a heading, a link or a picture
- divs, which are blocks with their own classes, and the callouts and tabs made from them
- figures, maths, diagrams and raw HTML
- shortcodes, which put other text into the page

Each section below shows the source of a feature, and then the result.

## .md and .qmd files

A page can be a `.md` file or a `.qmd` file. smalldocs reads both in the same way. A `.qmd` file is a
Markdown file that uses the additions above. The name `.qmd` comes from Quarto, and the additions come
from the Markdown of [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org), as Quarto uses it. So name a page `.qmd` to show
that it uses them. A Markdown viewer that does not know them, such as the file view of GitHub, shows
them as plain text.

A page can also be a Jupyter notebook, a `.ipynb` file. See [Notebooks](notebooks.ipynb).

## Front matter

Front matter is a block of YAML between two `---` lines at the top of a page. It holds the options of
the page:

```markdown
---
title: Writing pages
description: The Markdown that smalldocs reads.
order: 3
---
```

The title goes at the top of the page and in the sidebar. [The configuration](config.qmd) lists the
other options.

## Text

smalldocs changes some characters in text. To keep them as you type them, set the option
`from: markdown-smart`:

| You write | The page shows |
|---|---|
| `"quoted"` | "quoted" |
| `--` | -- |
| `---` | --- |
| `...` | ... |

Footnotes get numbers[^1]. Text can be ~~struck out~~, and `code` keeps its own characters.

[^1]: A footnote goes to the end of the page.

Term
: A definition list gives each term its definition.

- [x] A task list
- [ ] with boxes

## Headings and attributes

Each heading has an id, so a link can point at it, as in `config.qmd#globs`. smalldocs makes the id
from the text of the heading. The id is in lower case, with a `-` between the words. It keeps letters,
digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, and it drops other punctuation and anything before the first letter. So
`## A _quarto.yml` gets the id `a-_quarto.yml`. Pandoc makes ids by the same rules, so a link written for
Pandoc or Quarto still works.

To give your own id and classes, put them in braces:

```markdown
## Install it {#install .important}
```

A link, a picture, a span and inline code take attributes too. A span is text in brackets with
attributes after it. Write `[text](url){.btn .btn-primary}`,
`![alt](pic.png){width=50%}` or `[red]{.text-danger}`. Here is [a button](get-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-sm}
and a [span with a class]{.text-danger}.

## Divs

A div is a block of the page with its own attributes. A line of three or more colons starts or ends a
div. A line with attributes starts a div, and a line of colons only ends the innermost div. So divs can
nest, with lines of the same length:

```markdown
::: {.border .p-3}
Outer.

::: {.text-center}
Inner, in the centre.
:::
:::
```

::: {.border .p-3}
Outer.

::: {.text-center}
Inner, in the centre.
:::
:::

## Callouts

A callout is a box that sets off a note, a tip or a warning:

```markdown
::: {.callout-note}
A note, with the default title.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## A tip with its own title
The first heading in a callout becomes its title.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Folded" collapse="true"}
This warning opens when you click its title.
:::
```

::: {.callout-note}
A note, with the default title.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## A tip with its own title
The first heading in a callout becomes its title.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Folded" collapse="true"}
This warning opens when you click its title.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
An important callout. A caution callout comes next.
:::

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple"}
A caution with `appearance="simple"`.
:::

## Tabs

A tabset is a group of tabs. In a div with the class `panel-tabset`, each heading becomes a tab:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Python

```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    "Say hello."
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

## Shell

```bash
for name in Ann Bo; do echo "Hello, $name!"; done
```

## Prose

A tab can hold any Markdown.
:::

## Code

smalldocs colours code with [Pygments](https://pygments.org), in the light theme and in the dark
theme. See [Themes](themes.qmd). A copy button shows when the pointer is on the code. A `filename` goes above the code:

```{.python filename="hello.py"}
import sys

def main() -> int:
    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
        print(arg.upper())  # one line each
    return 0
```

A `diff` block shows a change to files, as `git diff` prints it. As on GitHub, smalldocs shows each
removed line in red and each added line in green. The `---` and `+++` lines that name the files are red
and green too. A hunk header, the line that starts with `@@`, is grey on a blue band. A `diff --git` or
`index` line is grey and bold. The other lines keep their text as written, with the space at their start.

The names `udiff` and `patch` do the same. In a combined diff from a merge, smalldocs colours only the
lines that start with `+` or `-`. Quarto and Pandoc colour a diff in the colours of strings and
variables, and not in red and green.

```diff
--- a/hello.py
+++ b/hello.py
@@ -3,3 +3,3 @@
 def main() -> int:
-    for arg in sys.argv:
+    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
         print(arg.upper())  # one line each
```

A code block whose fence names a language in braces, such as `{python}` or `{r}`, is a cell. A cell is
code that is meant to run when the page is built, with its output in the page. smalldocs does not run
code. It shows the cell as code, and the page shows no output. The build gives a warning for each page
with cells.

A cell can start with option lines that begin with `#|`. smalldocs removes these lines. It hides the
cell for `#| echo: false` or `#| include: false`. To hide every cell of a page, set `echo: false` in its
front matter.

## Raw HTML

HTML in the Markdown goes into the page unchanged. A block marked `{=html}` also goes in unchanged:

```{=html}
<p class="text-success">This paragraph came from a raw HTML block.</p>
```

## Figures

A picture alone in its paragraph becomes a figure, if it has alt text. The alt text becomes the
caption:

![The smalldocs mark, drawn as an SVG.](../images/mark.svg){width=120px}

## Tables

A table has a row of headings, a row of dashes, and a row for each line of the table. A `|` goes
between the cells:

| Feature | Written as | Note |
|---|---|---|
| A column | `\| a \|` | Put `\|` at both ends of each row |
| Alignment | `\|:---\|---:\|` | A colon sets the side |
| `\|` in a cell | `\\|` | A backslash before it |

smalldocs does not read the grid tables of Pandoc, which are drawn with `+` and `-`.

## The margin and wide content

The margin is the column at the right of the text, where the table of contents is. A note in the
margin stands beside the text that it belongs to. smalldocs reads the classes of Quarto for it.

::: {.column-margin}
This note is in a `.column-margin` div. It stands beside the paragraph below it.
:::

A div with the class `.column-margin` goes in the margin. It starts level with the next paragraph,
and it can hold any Markdown:

```markdown
::: {.column-margin}
A note in the margin.
:::
```

A span with the class `.aside` goes in the margin, level with its line. Write it as
`[a short note]{.aside}`, for example [a note from a span]{.aside} in this paragraph.

### Footnotes in the margin

To put each footnote in the margin, set `reference-location` in the config or in the front matter:

```yaml
reference-location: margin
```

Each footnote then goes beside the paragraph that cites it first, and not to the end of the page. The
links to the footnotes keep their anchors, `#fn1` and `#fnref1`, as in Quarto.

### Captions in the margin

To put the caption of each figure in the margin, set `fig-cap-location: margin`. For one figure,
give the attribute `fig-cap-location=margin` to the picture. A figure with the
class `.column-margin` goes in the margin itself, with its caption under it.

### Content wider than the text

A div with one of these classes is wider than the text:

| Class | Width |
|---|---|
| `.column-body-outset` | A little wider than the text, on both sides |
| `.column-page` | From a little left of the text to the right side of the margin |
| `.column-page-inset` | A little narrower than `.column-page` |
| `.column-screen` | The whole width of the window |
| `.column-screen-inset` | The width of the window, less a small space at each side |
| `.column-screen-inset-shaded` | The same, with a shaded background |

Each class except `.column-page-inset` and `.column-screen-inset-shaded` also has a `-left` and a
`-right` form, which is wide on one side only. A figure in such a div fills its width if the figure
has `width=100%`.

On a narrow screen, the content of the margin goes into the text, after the paragraph it belongs to.
Content for a wide column takes the width of the text. If margin or wide content passes under the
sidebar or the table of contents, that panel is hidden until the content has passed.

## Maths

Inline maths goes between dollars, as in $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$. Display maths goes between double dollars:

$$
\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx = \frac{1}{3}
$$

KaTeX, a JavaScript library, draws the maths. smalldocs loads KaTeX only on pages that have maths.

smalldocs reads a dollar as the start of maths when it has no digit before it and no space after it.
The maths ends at the next dollar in the paragraph. If that dollar has a space before it or a digit
after it, the first dollar is only a dollar. So the text "it costs $5 and $10" stays as it is. To keep
one dollar as a dollar, write `\$`.

For text with many prices, set the option `from: markdown-tex_math_dollars`, in the front matter or in
`_smalldocs.yml`. Then each dollar is a dollar, and smalldocs draws no maths written with dollars.

## Diagrams

The JavaScript library mermaid.js draws a `mermaid` block. smalldocs loads it only on pages that have a
diagram:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[_smalldocs.yml] --> B(smalldocs render)
  C[pages] --> B
  B --> D[_site]
```

## Shortcodes

A shortcode is a tag in double braces that smalldocs replaces before it reads the Markdown. smalldocs
replaces these shortcodes everywhere except in code blocks:

| Shortcode | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `{{</* include _part.qmd */>}}` | The file, without its front matter |
| `{{</* meta title */>}}` | An option of the page: {{< meta title >}} |
| `{{</* var version */>}}` | A value from `_variables.yml`, a YAML map of names to values at the root of the project |
| `{{</* env HOME */>}}` | An environment variable |

To show a shortcode as it is, put `/*` and `*/` inside its braces. The left column of the table does
so in its source.
